title: Learning from pit drummers and teaching himself harmony
summary: On trains and backstage he studies harmony books and practices softly between shows; theater drummers invited him home and taught him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: But it was a means, I was learning and during that time I WAS TRAVelling on trains -- I was studying harmony, and I taught myself to read, all during this period. I was getting it and I learned so much from drummers in the pit.
The drummers in the theaters in those days were very accomplished musicians, they play the shows, they could read, they played xylophones, they played timpanies, they were all round musicians.

Oh, yeah, they were all-around, that was part of the thing and they'd hear me between shows, the manager was always coming back and threatening to throw me out of the theater, because between shows when the picture was on, I'd be back there practicing between shows, see I'd get out of my clothes that I wore on stage in a bathroom and it'd be dark, maybe I'd get one little light backstage and I'd move my instrument over under that light. And I'd play, but I'd play it with soft hammers, but maybe they'd hear it --

Cause once in awhile you get the wrong hammer, you play a little loud. So they'd come back, come back stage and then after they said, 'Why don't you come out to my house, I got an instrument or something, after the theater act'd go out and we'd talk, maybe I'd stay there until 2:00 in the morning, we'd play, I'd learn from these guys.
So you got a real education with those guys?
I'd got so that I knew the notes and I --
-- I studied harmony out of books, I would buy books --
-- oh heck there's another book and chords and this sort of thing --

-- outside of that -- I never had any lessons. Outside of those probably 10 lessons I had from Leo Johnson in Jacksonville, in the very beginning, which showed me how to hold the hammers, mainly. Just basic things.
